In his later years, Einstein continued to work on a unified field theory, an attempt to reconcile the forces of electromagnetism and gravity, but he did not achieve a definitive theory before his death on April 18, 1955.

Albert Einstein's legacy is vast, extending beyond physics to influence philosophy, politics, and culture. His theories have provided the foundation for modern physics, influencing everything from quantum mechanics to cosmology.
